name: Amendio – Order Cancellation and Self-Service Changes for WooCommerce
author: mbishu

sections.description:
Every “can I change my order?” email is a customer who would rather have done it themselves. Amendio adds a Change order button to the order confirmation page and to My Account, and lets the customer do it, within a window and a set of permissions you control.

What customers can do:

  • Change size or option. Swap a line for another variation of the same product. Same price, nothing to pay; dearer, they pay the difference; cheaper, they get it back.
  • Change quantity. Fewer units refunds the difference as a real WooCommerce refund. More units creates a balance order they pay on your normal checkout.
  • Add to the order. Another option of something already on the order, shipped in the same box, with a pay link for the balance.
  • Change the delivery address. Validated against your shipping zones. Optionally allowed after shipping, flagged for you to pass to the carrier.
  • Cancel, with a reason. The customer says what went wrong before the order is cancelled. The refund goes back the way it came; manual gateways are flagged with the exact amount owed.

What you get: a dashboard of how many tickets the flow deflected, how many orders were cancelled and what the customers gave as the reason, so you can fix what is actually driving cancellations.

Every change is checked against the live order (stock, status, edit window, gateway) so nothing is offered that cannot actually be done, and every change is expressed in WooCommerce’s own money model: a paid order’s total is never edited, decreases are refunds with line items, increases are balance orders. Your reports, your gateway and your invoices agree.

No limits. Every feature works on every order, forever. There is no order quota, no trial and nothing switched off.

Works with the classic and block checkout, high-performance order storage (HPOS), guest orders, and any payment gateway that supports refunds through WooCommerce.

Runs on your site. Orders never leave your server.

More about the plugin, including screenshots of each flow, at amendio.app.

A separate commercial plugin, Amendio Premium, answers a cancellation with a counter-offer, adds product recommendations to the add-to-order screen, intercepts WooCommerce Subscriptions cancellations, and adds appearance controls. It is not part of this plugin and nothing here depends on it.
sections.installation:
1. Install from the Plugins screen, or upload the folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Amend settings, set the edit window and which changes you allow. The button appears on every eligible order page.

Shortcode for custom pages: [amend_change_order order="123"]
sections.faq:
How do customers cancel their own order in WooCommerce?

WooCommerce has no customer-facing cancel flow beyond the pending-payment state, so most stores handle it by email. Amendio adds a Change order button to the order confirmation page and to My Account. The customer picks a reason, and the cancellation runs against the live order: stock goes back, the refund is a real WooCommerce refund carrying the line items, and the reason is recorded for your dashboard. You set the window and which actions are allowed.

Why will WooCommerce not let me refund the full amount?

WooCommerce will not create a refund larger than the order total minus what has already been refunded, and that ceiling catches people out in a specific way. If you lower a paid order’s total to take an item off and then refund the difference, you have spent part of the allowance twice over: a 100.00 order reduced to 60.00 with 40.00 refunded leaves only 20.00 refundable, even though you are still holding 60.00 of the customer’s money. The fix is to leave the total alone and record the decrease as a refund with line items instead, which is what Amendio does.

Can customers change the size or variation on an order they have paid for?

Yes, within the window you set. The existing line is pointed at the new variation rather than being deleted and re-added, so the discount, the tax and the price already paid stay on it and the order total does not move. One unit of the old option goes back on the shelf and one of the new comes off it. If the new option costs more than they paid, the difference is a balance order they pay on your normal checkout rather than something the shop quietly absorbs.

Can customers change an order after it has shipped?

Item and quantity changes close the moment an order is marked shipped or completed, always. Address changes are closed by default too; you can allow them after shipping if your carrier accepts redirects, in which case the change is flagged on the order for you and the customer is told it is a request rather than a promise.

Which payment gateways work?

Any gateway that supports refunds through WooCommerce (Stripe, PayPal, WooPayments, Mollie, Square and most others) refunds automatically. Manual methods such as cash on delivery or bank transfer cannot refund themselves, so the order is flagged with the amount owed and the customer is told to expect a manual refund.

Does it change my order totals or reports?

No. A paid order’s total is never edited. Decreases are WooCommerce refunds with line items; increases are balance orders. Stock, tax and sales reports move the way they would if you had made the same change by hand.

Does it work with the block checkout and HPOS?

Yes. The customer panel renders on the classic and block order pages, and orders are read and written through the WooCommerce CRUD API, so high-performance order storage is supported.

Does it work for guest checkout?

Yes. The link on the order confirmation page and in the order email carries a signed key that only unlocks that order.

Is there a limit on orders?

No. Every feature works on any number of orders.

What data does it collect?

Nothing leaves your site. Cancel reasons and change attempts are stored in your own database, for your dashboard, and are deleted when you delete the plugin.

Can I change what the customer sees?

Yes. The panel is rendered from a WooCommerce template (change-order.php) you can override in your theme, and the flow exposes filters (amend_rules, amend_worth_offering, amend_next_steps, among others) for anything else.
sections.changelog:
1.1.3

  • Renamed in the directory to “Amendio – Order Cancellation and Self-Service Changes for WooCommerce”, and the tags rewritten against measured directory competition rather than guesswork. “edit order” and “woocommerce” were dropped because both are dominated by plugins with hundreds of thousands of installs and, in the case of “edit order”, by post-reordering plugins that have nothing to do with shop orders.
  • Tags are now: order cancellation, cancel order, cancellation reason, refund request, customer cancel order.
  • Three questions added to the FAQ, including why WooCommerce refuses to refund the full amount once an order total has been lowered.
  • No code changed. Nothing to do after updating.

1.1.2

  • The plugin’s row on the Plugins screen now links to the plugin site, the support forum and the review form.
  • Amend’s own admin screens carry those first two links in the footer line.
  • Once customers have made ten changes without a support ticket, one notice asks for a review. It appears on Amend’s screens only, never elsewhere in wp-admin, and does not come back once dismissed.
  • Nothing about the customer-facing flow changed.

1.1.1

  • Renamed in the directory to “Amendio – Self-Service Order Changes for WooCommerce”. The plugin folder, slug, settings and data are unchanged.
  • Tags changed to: cancel order, edit order, order cancellation, refund, woocommerce. Dropped: change address, customer self-service.
  • Added the Plugin URI and Author URI headers, both https://amendio.app/, so the Plugins screen and the directory page carry a link.
  • No code changed. Nothing to do after updating.

1.1.0

  • The plugin is now the complete free product: no licence checks, no gated code. Add-to-order is available to every store.
  • Compatible with WooCommerce 11.1.
  • Commercial features (counter-offers, recommendations, subscription retention, appearance) moved to a separate plugin.
  • Settings and dashboard rebuilt around what the free plugin does, with filters for extensions.

1.0.3

  • Directory release: plugin named Amendio, package cleanup, contributor account.

1.0.0

  • First release.
